body.heading: Lights that fly
paragraphs: On a warm summer evening, just as the sky turns purple, tiny lights begin to blink over the grass. On, off. On, off. They are fireflies — small beetles that can make their own light! A firefly's body has a special part near its tail that mixes chemicals together to make a glow. It is a cold light, not hot like a lamp or a candle, so the firefly never burns itself.
Each kind of firefly flashes in its own pattern, like a secret code made of light.

body.heading: Stop and think
paragraphs: Before you read on, think: why would a tiny beetle want to flash a light that other animals can see? Think of one reason — then read on and see if you were right.

body.heading: Talking with light
paragraphs: Fireflies flash to talk to each other. A male firefly flies above the grass, blinking his pattern. A female firefly waits below, and if she likes his pattern, she blinks back. That is how they find each other in the dark. But the flashes can also be a warning sign to birds and bats: 'I taste terrible — don't eat me!'

Sadly, fireflies are becoming harder to find in some places, because bright street lights confuse their signals and their grassy homes are being built over. Leaving a patch of long grass in a garden, and turning off outdoor lights, helps these tiny lanterns keep shining.

body.heading: Words to know
paragraphs: Glow — a soft, steady light, like the light a firefly makes.
Dusk — the time just after sunset, when the sky is still a little light but turning dark.
Signal — a sign or message sent to someone, like a flash that means 'I am here.'
Pattern — a design or order that repeats, like the firefly's blinking code.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. The firefly's flashes are both a message and a warning. What two different things do the flashes say?
2. If you wanted to help fireflies near your home, what could you do — and why would it help?

takeaway: Fireflies make their own cold light and flash in patterns to talk to each other — and we can help them by keeping dark, grassy places for them to live.
